answer: The effective federal funds rate averaged 19.04 percent in July 1981 (monthly average, not seasonally adjusted). Source: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System (H.15), read from FRED series FEDFUNDS.

The median sales price of houses sold in the U.S. was $442,600 in Q4 2022 (quarterly, not seasonally adjusted), as currently published. This is a revised figure; earlier vintages showed a higher value for that quarter (about $479,500, from memory, not re-checked). Source: U.S. Census Bureau / HUD, read from FRED series MSPUS.

The U.S. unemployment rate averaged about 3.7 percent over the 12 months of 2019 (3.675 percent, the simple mean of the seasonally adjusted monthly rates: 4.0, 3.8, 3.8, 3.7, 3.6, 3.6, 3.7, 3.6, 3.5, 3.6, 3.6, 3.6). Source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, read from FRED series UNRATE; the average is my calculation.

5 months of 2023: January through May. Year-over-year changes in the seasonally adjusted CPI-U were about 6.3% (Jan), 6.0% (Feb), 4.9% (Mar), 5.0% (Apr) and 4.1% (May). From June to December they were between 3.1% and 3.7%, below 4%. Source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, index levels read from FRED series CPIAUCSL; the year-over-year percentages are my calculation.

The highest weekly average 30-year fixed mortgage rate in 2023 was 7.79 percent, for the week of October 26, 2023 (Freddie Mac survey dated Thursday, 2023-10-26). Source: Freddie Mac Primary Mortgage Market Survey, read from FRED series MORTGAGE30US.

About 1.459 million jobs. Total nonfarm payroll employment (seasonally adjusted) rose from 156,857 thousand in December 2023 to 158,316 thousand in December 2024, a gain of 1,459 thousand, on the data as currently published (read 2026-10-10). Benchmark revisions have lowered this well below the roughly 2.0 to 2.2 million reported earlier (earlier figures from memory, not re-checked). Source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (Current Employment Statistics), read from FRED series PAYEMS; the difference is my calculation.

About 129.6 percent. The S&P CoreLogic Case-Shiller U.S. National Home Price Index (not seasonally adjusted, Jan 2000 = 100) rose from 134.157 in January 2012 to 308.055 in June 2022. Source: S&P Dow Jones Indices, read from FRED series CSUSHPINSA; the percent change is my calculation.

The most negative daily 10-year minus 2-year Treasury spread in 2023 was -1.08 percentage points, on July 3, 2023. The next lowest was -1.07 on March 8, 2023. Source: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis, calculated from Treasury constant maturity yields, read from FRED series T10Y2Y.

3 quarters, on currently published data: 2020 Q1 (-5.2%), 2020 Q2 (-28.0%) and 2022 Q1 (-1.0%), all seasonally adjusted annualized rates. 2022 Q2 was reported as negative in earlier vintages (from memory, not re-checked) but now shows +0.6%, so it does not count on current data. Source: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis, read from FRED series A191RL1Q225SBEA.

Seasonally adjusted initial jobless claims peaked at 6,137,000 for the week ending April 4, 2020, on currently published (revised) data. The week ending March 28, 2020 was next at 5,946,000. Original releases at the time showed a higher peak, in the week ending March 28 (about 6.87 million, from memory, not re-checked), before seasonal factors were revised. Source: U.S. Department of Labor, Employment and Training Administration, read from FRED series ICSA.
